answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to lock a stake before it can trade. Forging a thousand fake agents then costs a thousand deposits, and any identity caught cheating forfeits its stake, so mass forgery becomes a money-losing strategy. Honest agents meanwhile grow a reputation trellis: each completed exchange adds a verified link, letting others tell established participants from fresh shells. Picture the market as an orchard where each agent's pigment of trust is earned slowly through real work — uprooting it to plant a fake costs more than any fruit it could steal.
